chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said:

I asked al-Askari (peace be upon him) in al-Madinah about a man who bequeathed wealth in the way of Allah, and he said, 'The way of Allah is our Shiah.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned the way to reconcile this report with the report in which he said 'The way of Allah is the Hajj', that the meaning is that the wealth is given to a man from the Shiah to perform Hajj with it, so it fulfills both meanings together and the reports are saved from contradiction, and this is a good interpretation.

As for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hamdani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad who said: Ahmad ibn Hilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a Jew who died and bequeathed to their creditors, and he (peace be upon him) wrote, 'Deliver it to me and inform me so that I may execute it in what is appropriate, if Allah wills.' The first thing in this report is that it is very weak in chain of narrators because all its narrators are criticized, and specifically the author of the decree - Ahmad ibn Hilal - for he is famous for Ghuluw (exaggeration) and the curse, and what is specific to his narration we do not act upon. And even if it were safe from that, there would be no contradiction in it with what we presented from the reports because it is not more than that he ordered him to deliver the wealth to him to place it in its places, and it is not in it that when he sent the wealth to him he did not divide it among the creditors of the bequeathing Jew - rather - it is not impossible that he (peace be upon him) himself oversaw the distribution of that among them, for he (peace be upon him) is more knowledgeable about the manner of division among them and placing it in its places. And on this there is no contradiction between the reports, and he narrated this decree exactly.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Muhammad who said: Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a Jew who died and bequeathed to his creditors something that I am able to take, is it permissible for me to take it and deliver it to your mawalis, or execute it in what the Jew bequeathed? And he (peace be upon him) wrote, 'Deliver it to me and inform me of it so that I may execute it in what is appropriate, if Allah wills.' And we have explained the way in that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bequest from a Jew to his creditors according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent tension between the general definition of 'Sabil Allah' as the Shiah and specific bequests to non-Muslims by distinguishing between the spiritual essence of the path and the legal mechanism of distribution. He notes that while the Imam receives the funds to ensure they are placed in their proper stations, this does not preclude the wealth from fulfilling the deceased's legal obligations to their creditors, a nuance highlighted by the weak but non--contradictory report of Ahmad ibn Hilal. This scholarly approach preserves the integrity of both the theological definition and the practical jurisprudence of inheritance.
